Overdose Deaths EDA - Week 3 by Kyle Maher

Packages

library(tidyverse)
library(this.path)
library(readxl)
library(gt)
library(maps)
library(patchwork)
library(lubridate)
library(usmap)
library(scales)
set.seed(28)

Setup

Overdose Data

  • Remove columns with a constant value
    • “Period”
    • “Percent Complete”
  • Coalesce “Predicted Value” and “Data Value”
  • Rename to snake_case format
raw_overdose <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    dirname(this.path()),
    "..",
    "data",
    "VSRR_Provisional_Drug_Overdose_Death_Counts.csv"
  )
)

overdose <- raw_overdose %>%
  mutate(value = coalesce(`Predicted Value`, `Data Value`)) %>%
  select(
    -Period,
    -"Percent Complete",
    -Footnote,
    -"Footnote Symbol",
    -"Predicted Value",
    -"Data Value"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    state = "State Name",
    state_abbreviation = State,
    year = Year,
    month = Month,
    indicator = Indicator,
    percent_pending_investigation = "Percent Pending Investigation"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_year = my(paste(month, year)),
    state = as.factor(state),
    state_abbreviation = as.factor(state_abbreviation),
    year = as.integer(year),
    month = factor(month, levels = month.name, ordered = TRUE),
    indicator = as.factor(indicator),
    value = as.numeric(value),
    percent_pending_investigation = as.numeric(percent_pending_investigation)
  )

Population Data

  • Drop April 2021 estimates column
  • Use pivot_longer() to transform the year into one column
  • Remove the period before the state names
raw_pop <- read_excel(
  file.path(
    dirname(this.path()),
    "..",
    "data",
    "NST-EST2024-POP.xlsx"
  ),
  range = "A4:G62"
)

# Drop estimates, pivot year columns together, remove regions, remove period.
pop <- raw_pop %>%
  rename(state = "...1", base_estimates_april_2021 = "...2") %>%
  select(-base_estimates_april_2021) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `2020`:`2024`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "population"
  ) %>%
  mutate(state = sub("^\\.", "", state)) %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

State Data (For Region)

  • From the built in state.name and state.region
  • Add the states that appear in the Population Data
state <- data.frame(
  state = state.name,
  state_region = state.region
)

# Add states that appear in pop
odd_states <- data.frame(
  state =
    c("New York City",
      "District of Columbia",
      "Puerto Rico",
      "United States"),
  state_region = 
    c("Northeast", 
      "Northeast", 
      NA, 
      NA)
)

state <- bind_rows(state, odd_states)

state <- state %>%
  mutate(
    state = as.factor(state),
    state_region = as.factor(state_region)
  )

State Area

state_area <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    dirname(this.path()),
    "..",
    "data",
    "StateArea.csv"
  )
) %>%
  select("State and other areas2", "Land Area1") %>%
  rename(
    state = "State and other areas2",
    square_miles = "Land Area1"
  ) %>%
  slice(-(1:4)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(state)) %>%
  mutate(state = str_remove_all(state, "[0-9]")) %>%
  mutate(square_miles = str_remove_all(square_miles, ",")) %>%
  mutate(
    state = as.factor(state),
    square_miles = as.numeric(square_miles)
  )

State Unemployment Rate

state_unemployment <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    dirname(this.path()),
    "..",
    "data",
    "StateUnemploymentRate.csv"
  )
) %>%
  select(-Rank) %>%
  rename(
    state = "State",
    unemployment_rate = "August 2025(p)"
  ) %>%
  slice(-1) %>% # Remove Subheader row
  mutate(
    state = as.factor(state),
    unemployment_rate = as.numeric(unemployment_rate)
  )

Literacy Rates

state_literacy <- read_csv(
  file.path(
    dirname(this.path()),
    "..",
    "data",
    "us.-literacy-rates-by-state-2025.csv" # released 2025
  )
) %>%
  rename(
    state = state,
    literacy_score = "LiteracyRatesAverageLiteracyScore_2024"
  ) %>%
  select(state, literacy_score) %>%
  mutate(
    state = as.factor(state),
    literacy_score = as.numeric(literacy_score)
  )

Join Dataframes

df <- overdose %>%
  left_join(pop, by = c("state", "year")) %>%
  left_join(state, by = "state") %>%
  left_join(state_area, by = "state") %>%
  left_join(state_unemployment, by = "state") %>%
  left_join(state_literacy, by = "state") %>%
  mutate(state_lower = tolower(state))

Investigate Limits

Questions the Data Can Not Answer

  • Is there Seasonality?
    • The rolling sum removes any seasonality.
  • Which drug is most likely to overdose on?
    • No data on the number of users.
    • No data on doseage amounts.

Questions the Data Can Answer

  • Do states with a highter population density also have more overdoses?
  • Do states with a highter unemployment rate also have more overdoes?
  • Do states with a lower literacy rate also have more overdoeses?

However, checking these questions will not explain any causation, only correlation.

Setup for Correlations

Isolate Yearly Sum for 2024

Select the values for december of 2024, which are the sum from January through December for 2024.

df <- df %>%
  filter(month_year == "2024-12-01", !is.na(value)) %>%
  filter(
    state != "United States",
    state != "Puerto Rico",
    state != "New York City"
  )

Filtered Dataframe:

df %>%
  select(
    state, 
    population, 
    square_miles, 
    unemployment_rate, 
    literacy_score, 
    indicator, 
    value
  ) %>%

Control for Population

  • Use deaths per 100,000 people
df <- df %>%
  mutate(value = (value / population) * 100000)

Calculate State Population Density

  • Population per square mile
df <- df %>%
  mutate(population_density = (population / square_miles))

Calculate Pearson Correlations

Population Density

df %>%
  group_by(indicator) %>%
  summarise(
    correlation = cor(
      value, 
      population_density,
      method = "pearson",
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(correlation)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(
    columns = 2,
    fn = scales::col_numeric(
      palette = c("#F9F3EF", "#D2C1B6"),
      domain = NULL
    )
  ) %>%
  tab_options(table.align = "left") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Population Density vs Deaths by Indicator")

Common Correlations

Unemployment Rate

  • Cocaine (T40.5)

Population Density vs Cocaine Overdose Deaths

population_density <- plot_usmap(
  data = df, 
  values = "population_density", 
  regions = "states"
) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "inferno",
    trans = "log",
    breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x),
    labels = comma_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Population Density 2024 by State",
    fill = "Population Per Square Mile"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.1, "cm"),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 14, 
      face = "bold", 
      vjust = 5, 
      hjust = .5
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

cocaine_deaths <- plot_usmap(
  data = filter(df, indicator == "Cocaine (T40.5)"), 
  values = "value", 
  regions = "states"
) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "inferno",
    trans = "log",
    breaks = trans_breaks("log10", function(x) 10^x),
    labels = comma_format()
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Cocaine Overdose Deaths in 2024 by State",
    fill = "Count Per 100,000 People"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
    legend.key.size = unit(1.1, "cm"),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 14, 
      face = "bold", 
      vjust = 5, 
      hjust = .5
    ),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14)
  )

cocaine_deaths

Conclusion

Most of the correlations appeared as expected with a postitive correlaiton between Population Density and Overdose Deaths, a positive correlation between state Unemployment Rate and Overdose Deaths, and a negative correlation betweeen state Literacy Score and Overdose Deaths.

The strongest corelation was between population density and overdose deaths due to Cocaine with a correlation of .758.

All three factors considered were correlated significantly with the folowing two indicators: - Natural, semi-synthetic, & synthetic opioids, incl. methadone (T40.2-T40.4) - Synthetic opiods, excl. methadone (T40.4)
